candidates.observed_shape: A small solid oblique oval/dash, slanting down toward the right, with no clearly distinct descending comma tail or hook.
candidates.identity_rationale: The mark can be read as an oblique dot/dash rather than an unambiguous comma. A writer could use a short stroke as a comma in context, but this isolated generated form and the supplied punctuation-only composition do not establish a sufficiently readable comma identity.
candidates.uncertainty: Identity is ambiguous, rather than a proven alternative character. No alternative label is assigned. Rejection is a conservative current quality-gate decision, not a claim that no reader could infer a comma from context.
candidates.recommendation: Exclude this exact output from confidently approved comma coverage. A changed output or additional legitimate contextual evidence would need its own review; do not inherit acceptance from the receipt.

candidates.uncertainty: The intended training/style mechanism is not diagnosed here. The visible shape failure is unambiguous.
candidates.recommendation: Exclude this output from approved punctuation coverage and from quality-qualified composition. A new legitimate model output requires a new review; do not patch a ring onto this output to claim model success.

overall.summary: Full stop fails due to an open/incomplete ring; comma is an ambiguous oblique solid mark and is conservatively rejected for current quality-qualified use. Neither provenance success nor the complete training budget cures these visible output failures.
